Please note: We hope you are settling in well, for new parents, please have a look at our Parent tab - At a glance for more helpful information about the school......Eco-Schools award achieved for the fourth year running!......Check out our blog - School In Action, for all of our excellent day to day news - use the ´Quick Links´ in the top right hand corner of the website to access it
Here at the Polygon School we want to encourage and develop a motivation for learning that will stay with our students throughout their lives.
Our aim is that students are safe, healthy, happy and that they are engaged in our curriculum. We know that if we get this right, our students will make a positive contribution to society in the future.
We pride ourselves on the relationships that we have with our students and this is underpinned by our belief that students of the school should be valued and treated fairly regardless of their background or ability.
At The Polygon School, we aim to remove any barriers to learning and give our students a positive educational experience that can then lead them on to success in the future.
Mr B Penfold, Headteacher

SEND Information
Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND)
Our SENDCO is: Miss Gemma Griffiths ​​​​​​gemma.griffiths@polygon.southampton.sch.uk
Supporting Pupils with Special Needs at The Polygon School
Every pupil who attends the school has an Education Health and Care Plan (EHCP). This is a legal document issued by the Local Authority which gives each pupil entitlement to education and to have their special needs met at our school. We are a school for young people with Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs. These needs alongside any additional needs are clearly stated on their EHCPs. The plans state how we, along with Health and Social Care (if appropriate), work to meet the needs of our young people. The plans contain desired outcomes that we work towards within the provision that we offer at the school.
Every young person has an Annual Review meeting each year to review their progress towards meeting the desired outcomes on their EHCPs. The Annual Review is a meeting that is held at school with the young person's parent(s) / carer(s), tutor and Gemma Griffiths the SENDCO (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Coordinator) pus any other professionals who are involved with the plan. We aim for the young person to attend some of the meeting too, if they are able to do so. The voices of all parties are fully taken into account in reviewing the plan. - https://www.polygon.southampton.sch.uk/annual-reviews/
In order to scaffold success for all of our pupils in the areas of both their behaviour and learning, each pupil has two specific targets that they work on every term. Success with these targets is measured in every lesson that takes place within the school day. Points are earned and the pupils can trade in their points for a variety of rewards that are motivating to our young people.
To further support some of our young people we are able to refer to an Occupational Therapist and a Speech & Language Therapist who are shared with other SEMH provisions within the city. We can also access support through referring to the School Nursing Team. We directly employ a Counsellor who works 1:1 and with some small groups on two days per week.
If you have any questions about SEND at our school please don't hesitate to get in touch with Gemma Griffiths (SENDCO).

Southampton Co-operative Learning Trust
The Southampton Co-operative Learning Trust provides education for over 3000 children and their families in the local area. Alongside us in the Trust are; Banister Primary School, Foundry Lane Primary School, Freemantle C of E Community Academy, Regents Park Community College and St John's Nursery and Primary School and St Mark’s C of E School.
The Trust has a shared identity through our commitment to safe and secure environments which strengthen and sustain high standards and achievement for the communities we serve.

Curriculum
At The Polygon School we have developed a curriculum to meet the individual needs of our students which provides them with the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to be successful and progress positively to their next steps.
*If you would like further information about our curriculum, please see the individual subject areas below or contact the school.
Many of our students join us following a disrupted or challenging period in their education, making re-engagement with learning a key priority within our curriculum.
We design pathways that are carefully tailored to meet the individual needs outlined in each student’s EHCP. By capturing their interest and imagination, we aim to foster a positive and supportive learning environment where every student feels included, understood, and valued.
To help overcome barriers to learning, we take a relational and trauma-informed approach. Personal development is embedded throughout our curriculum, helping to build students’ confidence, strengthen trust in staff, and support the development of essential life skills both in and beyond the classroom.
Our curriculum is designed to inspire students by nurturing curiosity, promoting aspiration, and opening doors to new possibilities. We place a strong emphasis on developing cultural capital, ensuring students have access to enrichment opportunities that broaden their horizons and build their confidence in the wider world.
Through meaningful employer encounters, we help students explore future pathways and raise their ambitions for life beyond school. We are committed to improving reading and oracy, recognising them as essential skills for learning, communication, and participation in society.
We believe that all our students can achieve, while recognising that each has unique needs, strengths, and starting points. Our aim is to ensure every student is well-prepared for their next steps in life. To support this, we have developed a carefully sequenced curriculum that offers a range of appropriate academic qualifications, while also prioritising personal development. Our approach enables pupils to know more, remember more, and do more, equipping them with the skills and knowledge they need to thrive both now and in the future.
We actively celebrate success, academic, personal, and social to build self-belief, encourage resilience, and foster a strong sense of pride and achievement. Ultimately, we aim to instil a love of learning and a mind-set geared towards lifelong learning.

Annual Reviews
Each year parents/carers and relevant professionals will be invited to attend an annual review of your young person's Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). This pupil-centred process will allow you and your young person to share how the previous year has gone, discussing all aspects of school life both the positives and areas for development. It will also give you both a chance to discuss the future to ensure that any plans made are focused on improving your young person’s outcomes.
Gemma Griffiths (SENDCO) and your young person’s tutor will share the progress that has been made and how the school will make provisions for ensuring that they arebest placed to meet their potential. A representative from the Special Educational Needs and Disabilities 0-25 Service may also attend the meeting to offer support and advice. After the meeting, an annual review report will be compiled by the SENDCO and copies will be sent to the local authority Special Educational Needs and Disabilities 0-25 Service and to parents/carers.
